notes.text: The first man. The LORD God formed him of the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul (Genesis 2:7). He was made, not born — the chapter gives him no mother and no father, so his parent fields are set to "none", not "unknown": affirmatively no parents, not a missing record. He is also the only human formed in this chapter, and God calls him "alone" before making the woman (Genesis 2:18), so his sibling state is "none" as well. God, who acts throughout the chapter, is not a person record in the tree.

quotes.text: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.

notes.text: The LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden and put the man there to dress it and to keep it (Genesis 2:8 and Genesis 2:15). Then came the first command: of every tree of the garden he may freely eat, but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil he must not eat — in the day he eats of it he shall surely die (Genesis 2:16-17).

quotes.text: And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.

notes.text: The first verse where the KJV calls him by name: the beasts of the field and the fowls of the air are brought "unto Adam to see what he would call them", and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, "that was the name thereof" (Genesis 2:19). Every earlier verse calls him only "the man", so Genesis 2:19 is recorded as his first mention. He named the cattle, the fowl and every beast, but among them "there was not found an help meet for him" (Genesis 2:20) — no companion, which sets up the woman.

quotes.text: And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof.
And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.

notes.text: To fix his being alone, a deep sleep falls on Adam; the LORD God takes one of his ribs, closes up the flesh instead of it, builds the rib into a woman and brings her to him (Genesis 2:21-22). Adam answers with the first recorded human words: "This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh" — "she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man" (Genesis 2:23). She is called Woman here, but her proper name Eve is not stated until Genesis 3:20, which has not been walked yet, and a person enters the tree only at the verse where their name is stated — so she is not on the tree yet. When Genesis 3 is walked she will be added there and linked to Adam as his wife.

quotes.text: And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.
And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.

notes.text: The chapter records his marriage: "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh" (Genesis 2:24), and the two of them were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed (Genesis 2:25). His wife is not in the tree yet — her name is first stated at Genesis 3:20 — so his spouse list is empty and marked "unknown" as a walk-in-progress placeholder; the marriage will be drawn on the tree once she enters.

quotes.text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.
